problems.problem: Let $n$ be any positive integer other than $2$, $3$ or $5$. Show that a square can be cut into exactly $n$ smaller squares (which may be of different sizes).
A function $f$ satisfies $$f(x)+xf(1-x)=x$$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine $f(2)$ and find a formula for $f$.
Find four prime factors of the number $3^{32}-2^{32}$ which are less than $100$.
If $x$, $y$ and $z$ are real numbers in the interval $[-2,1]$ and $x+y+z=0$, show that $$x^2+y^2+z^2\le6.$$

In the triangle $ABC$, $\angle ABC=2\angle ACB$. Prove that
(a) $AC^2=AB^2+AB\cdot BC$,
(b) $AB+BC<2AC$.
Show, for all integers $n>1$, that the sum $$\frac11+\frac12+\frac13+\dots+\frac1n$$ is not an integer.
Find all pairs $(a,b)$ of nonnegative integers which satisfy the equation $$2^a\cdot3^b-3^{b+1}+2^a=13.$$

The vertices of a cube are numbered with the numbers from $1$ to $8$ (each number used once). For each edge, the sum of the numbers at its endpoints is formed. Is it possible to number the vertices in such a way that the sums for the edges are all different?

In the triangle $ABC$, a point $P$ divides the side $AB$ in the ratio $\frac{AP}{PB}=\frac14$. The perpendicular bisector of the segment $PB$ meets the side $BC$ at the point $Q$. Find $BC$ if it is known that $AC=7$ and $F(PQC)=\frac{4}{25}F(ABC)$, where $F(XYZ)$ denotes the area of the triangle $XYZ$.

Every day Jóhanna runs either $a$ kilometres or $b$ kilometres, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers and $a>b$. Jóhanna can run exactly $100$ kilometres in $9$ days or in $11$ days, but not in $10$ days. Find all possible values of $a$ and $b$.
Find all integers $a$ and $b$ such that $(a^3+b)(a+b^3)=(a+b)^4$.

The allowed moves from one positive integer to another are as follows:
(a) From $n$ one may go to $2n$ and back.
(b) From $n$ one may go to $3n+1$ and back.
Prove that, wherever the moves start, one can always reach $1$ with finitely many moves.
Find all pairs of real numbers $p$ and $r$ which solve the equations $$p+pr+pr^2=28,$$ $$p^2r+p^2r^2+p^2r^3=224.$$

The rectangle $PQRS$ represents an A4 sheet, that is, $PQ:PS=\sqrt2:1$. The rectangle (the sheet) is folded so that the corner $Q$ lands on the point $X$ on the side $SR$ and the fold line $PY$ passes through the point $P$. The length of the side $PS$ is $1$. Find the side lengths of the triangle $RXY$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/iceland_2012_p2_fig.png
Prove that among any five integers one can always find two of them such that either their sum or their difference is divisible by $7$.
Find all positive integers $m$ and $n$ such that $m$ divides $2n-1$ and $n$ divides $2m-1$.

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$, the angles $\angle ADC$ and $\angle BCD$ are greater than $90^\circ$; $F$ is the intersection point of the line $AC$ and the line through $B$ parallel to $AD$, and $E$ is the intersection point of the line $BD$ and the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$. Prove that $EF$ is parallel to $CD$.

100 lamps form a square which is 10 lamps wide and 10 lamps high. Each lamp has a button. If the button on some lamp is pressed, all lamps in the same column and all lamps in the same row, as well as the lamp itself, change state, i.e. those that were off are switched on and those that were on are switched off. (Lamps which are neither in the same row nor in the same column remain unchanged meanwhile.)
For which initial states is it possible to switch on all the lamps? In other words, which lamps may be on and which off at the start so that, by pressing the switches, one can end up with all the lamps lit?
Let $a,b,c,d,e,f$ and $g$ be distinct positive integers less than or equal to $7$. Find all primes which can be written in the form $$a\cdot b\cdot c\cdot d+e\cdot f\cdot g.$$

In the trapezoid $ABCD$ the opposite sides $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel, $|AB|=a$, $|CD|=b$, and the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at the point $E$. The segment $FG$ passes through $E$ parallel to $AB$ and has its endpoints on the sides $BC$ and $AD$. Express $|FG|$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.

A circle is divided into $n$ equal arcs. The numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ are distributed on the arcs (one number on each arc) so that the number of arcs between the numbers $a$ and $a+1$ is always the same, for all $a$ from $1$ to $n-1$. The numbers $11$, $4$ and $17$ fall, in this order, on adjacent arcs. Find the number $n$ and justify why this is the only possibility.

In the acute triangle $ABC$, $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ are the altitudes to the corresponding sides and $H$ is their intersection point. Show that the following equation holds: $$\frac{|AH|}{|AD|}+\frac{|BH|}{|BE|}+\frac{|CH|}{|CF|}=2.$$
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $$\sqrt{\frac{9n-1}{n+7}}$$ is a rational number.
Find all pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ with $a\le b$ such that $$\left(a+\frac6b\right)\left(b+\frac6a\right)=25.$$
An equilateral triangle $RST$ is inscribed in an equilateral triangle $ABC$ so that $RS$ is perpendicular to $AB$. Find the area of $RST$ in terms of the area of $ABC$.
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $$n=d_2^2+d_3^3,$$ where $1=d_1<d_2<d_3$ are the smallest divisors of $n$.

Let $C$ be a circle with centre $M$ and let $P\ne M$ be a point in the plane. Every line which passes through $P$ and meets the circle $C$ determines a chord of the circle. Show that the midpoints of all these chords lie on one and the same circle.

Find all sequences of positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ such that the following hold:
1) $a_{m+n}-1$ divides $a_m+a_n$ for all $m$ and $n$.
2) $n^2-a_n$ is the square of an integer for all $n$.

We have an $8\times8$ chessboard and plenty of pawns. In how many different ways can one choose squares on the board and put one pawn on each chosen square so that the number of pawns in every row and every column is odd?
Show that the product of two adjacent numbers of the sequence $t_n=n(n+1)$ with $n\in\mathbb{N}$ gives a result which also belongs to the sequence.
The triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle of radius $R$. Show that $$|AB|\cdot|AC|=2R\cdot h_{BC},$$ where $h_{BC}$ is the altitude of the triangle to the side $BC$.

The front row of a cinema hall has 10 seats, all occupied. Everybody goes out during the intermission, and after the intermission each person sits either in his or her previous seat or in a seat next to his or her previous seat. In how many ways can the people of the front row take their seats after the intermission?
Show that there are infinitely many triples of natural numbers $(a,b,c)$ such that $$a^2+b^2+1=c^2.$$
Find the largest value of $\frac{x}{y}$ if the equation $$(x-3)^2+(y-3)^2=6$$ holds for the pair of real numbers $(x,y)$.

Gutti chooses positive integers $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ with $n>1$ and keeps them secret. Jörmunrekur wants to find out their values. Gutti allows Jörmunrekur to choose some $n$ positive integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ as often as he likes, and each time Gutti tells him the value of the sum $a_1x_1+a_2x_2+\dots+a_nx_n$. At least how many times does Jörmunrekur have to choose new numbers in order to succeed in his intention of determining the numbers $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$, regardless of which numbers Gutti chose?

An A4 sheet is divided into six parts or into sixteen parts. Some one of the parts is then divided into six or sixteen parts. This process may be repeated again and again. Is it possible that the number of pieces of paper, after a division, is at some stage equal to $2017$?

Gutti is a prankster. He divides when he is supposed to multiply, and he adds when he is supposed to subtract. Once Gutti was asked to subtract the number $60$ from the product of two natural numbers. By chance Gutti got the correct result. What could that result have been? Find all possibilities.

Andri Dagur and Björt Nótt sit at an ordinary chessboard ($8\times8$). In the bottom left corner stands a single rook. They take turns, and in each move they must move the rook to another square, as far as they like, above or to the right of the square on which it stands. The game ends when the rook has reached the top right corner. Andri starts. If getting the rook to the top right corner means
(a) a win,
(b) a loss,
which of them has, in each case, a winning strategy?
Find all real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $$x^2+x=y^3-y,$$ $$x^3-x=y^2+y.$$

The triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $AC=31$ and $AB=22$. The medians $CC'$ and $BB'$ are perpendicular to each other. Find the length of $BC$. (A median is determined by a vertex of the triangle and the midpoint of the opposite side.)
Find the value of the sum $xy+xz+yz$ if it is given that $$x^2+xy+y^2=1,$$ $$x^2+xz+z^2=2,$$ $$y^2+yz+z^2=3.$$ Here it suffices to find one solution.
Find all positive integers $x$ and $y$ such that $\sqrt{xy+2019}=\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{2019}$.

If $n$ is a positive integer, then $s(n)$ denotes the integer obtained by reversing the order of the digits that form $n$. For example, $s(2019)=9102$. How many positive two-digit integers $n$ are there such that $n+s(n)$ is a perfect square?

The triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $7$, $8$ and $9$. A line which contains the centre of the inscribed circle and is parallel to the shortest side of the triangle meets the other two sides of the triangle at the points $D$ and $E$. What is the length of the segment $DE$?

Among 25 horses we want to find the three fastest. We have no clock, but a racetrack where we can let five horses run at a time and see in which order they finish. Assume that every horse runs at a constant speed and that all of them have different speeds. Show that it is possible to find the three fastest horses and their order among themselves in seven races.
Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f(1)=2$ and $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)-f(x+y)+1$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$.

You are standing in front of a 31-storey building with two identical glass balls. You know that if you throw such glass balls from the 31st floor of the building down to the ground, they break. In the building there is a floor $n$ such that if the balls are thrown down from floor $n$ they break, and likewise if they are thrown from all floors above it (if there are any), but if they are thrown down from the floors below floor $n$ (if there are any), they do not break. Your task is to describe a method which guarantees that you find $n$ in as few throws as possible, no matter where in the building floor $n$ is.
Note: You may throw each ball as often as you like from any floor of the building until it breaks, but a broken ball is out of the game.
Gutti intends to colour each face of a cube either red or blue. How many different cubes can Gutti end up with?
In the acute triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $A$ and $E$ is the foot of the altitude from $B$. Show that the triangles $ABC$ and $DEC$ are similar.
How many four-digit numbers $n=\overline{abcd}$ ($a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are the digits of $n$) are there such that $a>d$ and the difference $\overline{abcd}-\overline{dcba}$ is a palindrome?
It is given that the polynomial $$P(x)=30x^4+17x^3-137x^2+13x+60$$ has roots $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$ and $r_4$. What is the value of the product $(1+r_1)(1+r_2)(1+r_3)(1+r_4)$?
In the plane there are $2021$ points, some black and the others green. Every black point is at distance $2021$ from exactly two green points. What is the least possible number of green points?
For which primes $p$ is $1+p+p^2+p^3$ a perfect square?
Are there three three-digit positive integers which have all nine digits different and which add up to $2022$?
Find distinct positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ such that $$\frac1a+\frac1b=\frac1c$$ and such that the quantity $a+b^2+c^3$ is as small as possible.
What is the largest number of pieces that can be obtained when a circular disc is divided by $6$ straight lines?

Atli and Fanney play a game on a rectangular board. They start with an empty board and move alternately. A move consists of a player colouring one or more cells which all lie in the same row or the same column. Each cell may be coloured only once. The player who colours the last cell wins. Atli starts.
(a) Which of them has a winning strategy on a $4\times6$ board?
(b) Which of them has a winning strategy on a $5\times6$ board?

A circle $\Omega$ and a point $A$ on $\Omega$ are given. Another point $B$ lies on the circle $\Omega$, and the circle $\Gamma_1$ with centre $B$ and radius $|AB|$ meets $\Omega$ again at $C$. The circle $\Gamma_2$ with centre $A$ and radius $|AC|$ meets $\Gamma_1$ again at $D$. Show that the line $AD$ is tangent to $\Omega$.

Let $a\in\mathbb{Q}_+$ be given. Determine all functions $f\colon\mathbb{Q}_+\to\mathbb{Q}_+$ such that for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}_+$ $$f\left(\frac xy+y\right)=\frac{f(x)}{f(y)}+f(y)+ax.$$ The set $\mathbb{Q}_+$ is the set of all positive rational numbers.
Let $p$ and $d$ be natural numbers such that $p$, $p+d$ and $p+2d$ are primes and $p\ge5$. Show that then $d$ is a multiple of $6$.
Find all triples of integers $(a,b,c)$ which satisfy the system of equations $$\begin{cases}a-bc=1\\ac+b=2.\end{cases}$$

Anna and Baldur play a game which starts with $n$ stones on a table. They move alternately and Anna starts. In each turn a player must take $1$ to $10$ stones from the table. The player who takes the last stone from the table wins. Anna starts. For which $n$ does Baldur have a winning strategy?

Let $\Gamma$ be a circle and $A$, $B$ and $C$ three points on the circle such that $\triangle ABC$ is acute. The altitude from $A$ meets $\Gamma$ again at the point $D$, and the altitude from $B$ meets $\Gamma$ again at the point $E$. Show that $\angle ACB=60^\circ$ if $|AB|=|DE|$.

At a chess tournament there are 12 participants, and every participant plays one game against each of the others. In each game the winner receives $1$ point and the loser $0$ points, while in case of a draw each receives $\frac12$ point. After the tournament the total score of each participant is computed. Tiebreak points are also computed in order to distinguish between participants with the same total score. To compute the tiebreak points of a participant, one adds up the total scores of those he defeated and half of the total scores of those he drew with.
For example, if a participant draws with an opponent who had a total score of $5$, this contributes $\frac12\cdot5$ to the participant's tiebreak points. If, on the other hand, he wins, it contributes $5$ to the participant's tiebreak points.
Show that the sum of all tiebreak points can be at most $363$.
Show that for $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>0$, $b>0$ and a positive integer $n$, $$\frac{a^n+a^{n-1}b+\dots+ab^{n-1}+b^n}{n+1}\le\frac{a^n+b^n}{2}.$$
Find all real numbers $x$, $y$ which satisfy both equations $$x^3+y^3=9\quad\text{and}\quad x^2y+xy^2=6.$$

Jörmunrekur has made a strip consisting of $89$ cells in a row. On each of the first $44$ cells from the left he puts one white stone. He then puts a black stone on each of the $44$ rightmost cells. He now intends to move the stones by making the following moves:
• A white stone may be moved one cell to the right if that cell is empty.
• A black stone may be moved one cell to the left if that cell is empty.
• A white and a black stone which are next to each other may be swapped if the white one is on the left.
It always takes the same number of moves to reach a position in which no more moves are possible. How many moves does it take?

Let $\gcd(a,b)$ denote the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$, i.e. the largest positive integer which divides both $a$ and $b$. Let $\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$ denote the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$, i.e. the smallest positive integer which both $a$ and $b$ divide. Find all positive integer solutions of the equation $$\gcd(a,b)+\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)=a+b.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid in which the side $AB$ is parallel to the side $DC$. Let $X$ be the intersection point of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Draw the line $\ell$ through $X$ parallel to $AB$. Let $Y$ and $Z$ be the intersection points of $\ell$ with the sides $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $a$ be the length of the side $AB$ and $b$ the length of the side $DC$. Show that the length of the segment $YZ$ is $\frac{2ab}{a+b}$.

On Línugata street there are $n$ houses numbered from $1$ to $n$, and in every house the lights are on. On each of $n$ days an elf intends to come to town. If an elf comes on day $i$, he flips the light switch of every house whose house number is divisible by $i$, so if the light was on it is off afterwards and vice versa. After the $n$ days the lights are still on in all houses except the first one, because some elves skipped coming to town in order to minimise traces. On which days did elves come to town?
Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the natural numbers, $0$ included. Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $$f(f(n))+f(n)=2n+3k$$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

There are ten boxes containing nine numbers; the last box is empty. A number may be moved from its box into the empty box. This counts as one operation. After that, the box in which the number was has become empty. Initially the order of the numbers is $8,7,3,9,1,5,2,6,4$. What is the least number of operations needed to get the numbers in increasing order, with the empty box last again? Why can it not be done in fewer operations than that?
Find all positive real numbers $x$ such that $$\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+91}=91.$$

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given. Let $X$ be the intersection point of its diagonals and assume that $X$ is inside $ABCD$. Let $[PQR]$ denote the area of the triangle with vertices $P$, $Q$ and $R$. Show that $$[ABX]\cdot[DCX]=[BCX]\cdot[DAX].$$

Benni's family, which is a family of $n\ge1$ people, regularly watches shows together. What they watch depends on who is present, so every (nonempty) subset of the family must be assigned shows to watch. To avoid repetition, two subsets may not watch the same shows if they intersect. At least how many series does the family need to find?

Let an integer $m\ge3$ be given. Call an integer $x$ good if $m\mid(x-1)$ and $m(m-1)\mid x(x-1)$. Here $a\mid b$ means that $a$ divides $b$ without remainder, i.e. $b=a\cdot k$ for some integer $k$. How many good numbers greater than $0$ and less than $m(m-1)$ are there if $m=2025$? And what about general $m$?
Fix an integer $k>0$. Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{Z}_+\to\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for all $n>0$ $$f(f(n))=n+k.$$
